raw_response:
I farm only 8.5 mu, and my house has seven people, but not everyone is on the farm full time, so I will keep the plan steady and labor-manageable. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm and it fits my experience, my irrigation well, and the local climate in Quzhou County. I will keep a smaller area in cotton because cotton still gives me a way to spread risk, but I will not let it take too much land because it needs more field watching and more spraying. I will also keep a small mungbean area because it is simple, short-season, and useful for cash and for spreading weather and market risk. Since I have well irrigation, I will not farm too conservatively on water, but I still will not push inputs too high because my land is not large and I want stable returns more than chasing the highest yield. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stand establishment, keep fertilizer moderate and practical, irrigate the grain crops more reliably than mungbean, and use rotary tillage because it is faster and easier for me to manage across the year.
